title: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC)
summary: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) is a university in Champaign. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with UIUC.

sections.heading: What UIUC is known for
paragraphs: The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) is a public research university known for its large and diverse undergraduate enrollment, which totals over 36,000 students. The institution maintains a selective admission rate of approximately 42%, reflecting its competitive academic environment. UIUC offers a wide range of programs, with notable shares in health-related fields and business studies, accounting for about 3.9% and 9.5% of the student body, respectively. These characteristics highlight UIUC's commitment to providing comprehensive education across various disciplines while serving a substantial student population.

sections.heading: Key strengths
paragraphs: The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) is a public institution recognized for its diverse academic offerings and commitment to accessible education. Approximately 3.9% of its programs focus on health-related fields, reflecting an investment in healthcare education. Additionally, education programs constitute about 2.5% of the university's academic portfolio, underscoring its dedication to training future educators. As a public university, UIUC emphasizes broad access and service to the community through its varied program strengths.

sections.heading: Popular majors
paragraphs: The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) offers a variety of popular majors that attract a diverse student body. Computer-related programs represent the largest share, accounting for approximately 9.7% of the academic offerings. Business majors follow closely, comprising about 9.5% of the programs. Health-related fields make up nearly 3.9%, while education programs account for around 2.5%. Public administration is also represented, though it constitutes a smaller portion at approximately 0.8%. These distributions illustrate UIUC's broad academic scope and its ability to cater to students with varied interests.

sections.heading: Student population
paragraphs: The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) has an undergraduate enrollment of 36,258 students, reflecting its status as a large public research university. Among this population, approximately 1.22% are aged 25 or older, indicating a predominantly traditional college-age demographic. Additionally, about 24.9% of undergraduates are first-generation college students, highlighting UIUC's role in providing access to higher education for students from diverse backgrounds.

sections.heading: Undergraduate admissions
paragraphs: The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) maintains a selective undergraduate admissions process with an admission rate of approximately 42.37%. Prospective students typically present competitive academic credentials, including an average SAT score of 1440. UIUC evaluates applicants based on a comprehensive review of their academic achievements and potential contributions to the campus community. While specific details about the use of the Common Application or early decision options are not provided, the university's admissions process aims to identify students who demonstrate strong academic preparation and alignment with the institution's educational goals.

sections.heading: How to read UIUC tuition
paragraphs: The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) tuition varies depending on residency status. In-state students pay $16,004 annually for tuition, reflecting the reduced rate for residents of Illinois. Out-of-state students are charged a higher tuition fee of $35,124 per year. The overall cost of attendance, which includes tuition, fees, housing, meals, and other expenses, totals $33,642. Understanding these figures helps prospective students and families plan financially for attending UIUC.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) offers financial aid to assist students in managing the cost of attendance. Approximately 23.41% of students receive Pell Grants, which are federal subsidies for low-income undergraduates. Among students who complete their degrees, the median debt is $19,500, indicating the typical loan amount borrowed. Prospective students can use the net price calculator available on the university's official website at www.illinois.edu/ to estimate their individual costs and aid eligibility. Additional financial data and resources are also accessible through the College Scorecard at https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/school/?145637.

sections.heading: Career outcomes
paragraphs: The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) demonstrates strong career outcomes for its graduates. The completion rate within 150% of the expected time is approximately 85.13%, indicating that a significant majority of students finish their programs on time. Graduates experience favorable earnings, with median salaries reaching $64,802 six years after enrollment and increasing to $81,054 ten years after enrollment. These figures suggest that UIUC alumni tend to see substantial income growth as they advance in their careers. Additionally, the median debt for students who complete their degrees is $19,500, reflecting the typical loan burden carried by graduates. These data points collectively highlight UIUC's effectiveness in supporting student success and long-term financial outcomes.

sections.heading: Diversity
paragraphs: The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) exhibits a diverse student body with a gender distribution of approximately 52% men and 48% women. The racial and ethnic composition includes about 37.53% White students, 5.31% Black students, 14.41% Hispanic students, and 23.11% Asian students. This demographic variety reflects UIUC's commitment to fostering an inclusive campus environment. Additionally, around 23.41% of students receive Pell Grants, indicating a significant portion of the student population comes from lower-income backgrounds. These figures highlight UIUC's efforts to support diversity and accessibility within its academic community.
